app_hypernet_explorer.title: App: Hypernet Explorer
app_hypernet_explorer.description: The browser, and it is a real one. Tabs with their own history each, back, forward, stop, refresh and home, an address bar with autocomplete, a links bar, an explorer bar with search, favorites and history, find on page, view source, saving a page into the file system, downloads, print preview and page setup, zoom, text size, encoding, a pop up blocker (with real pop ups when you turn it off), mail and news, synchronize, connection status, options, help, tip of the day, about, and a 404 gateway page that suggests what you might have meant. Every page in the archive is a real document. Preferences, favorites, history and downloads live in the OS registry, so they are kept in your savegame. The archive is where a great deal of this world explains itself. Read it.

app_my_computer.title: App: My Computer
app_my_computer.description: The file explorer. It browses the virtual file system: drives, folders, My Documents, and everything you or an application has written. Files opened here hand off to whichever application owns them, so a text file opens in Notepad and a saved web page opens in the browser.

app_notepad.title: App: Notepad
app_notepad.description: A plain text editor. It writes into the virtual file system, which means notes you type here are saved in your savegame and can be reopened, and read by any other application that reads files. It is the practical way to keep something you want to remember without leaving the machine.

app_control_panel.title: App: Control Panel
app_control_panel.description: Settings for the machine, plus a joke that turns out to be a readout: your party's statistics are presented as HARDWARE SPECIFICATIONS. Wallpapers, display settings and the rest of the machine's configuration live here too. Everything you change is stored in the registry and stays changed.

app_tv_guide.title: App: TV Guide
app_tv_guide.description: The television listings. It reads the broadcast database and lets you browse every channel, its cast and its programmes. Selecting a programme plays its broadcast inline, a line every couple of seconds, without leaving the desktop, so you can watch television on the computer. The schedule is regenerated every in game week and is fixed for that week, but the script never is: every tune in rerolls the broadcast.

app_the_object_index.title: App: The Object Index
app_the_object_index.description: The archive's catalogue of every object known to exist: one dossier per item, around eleven hundred of them, with all of its declared metadata laid open. The left page is the catalogue, grouped by category, with a search box. The right page is the dossier: identification, the archive's lore paragraph, commerce, physical properties, provisioning values, composition and the raw declaration tags. The lore paragraph is combinatorial: the world seed decides which words come out. The Randomize button rerolls that decision for this window only. It never changes the item's real description anywhere else in the game, and closing the app forgets it.

app_npolice.title: App: N€police
app_npolice.description: The continental police portal, and the way to deal with your own criminal record without waiting to be caught. Three pages: - CASE FILE, every charge with its fine, settleable one at a time or all at once. Settling clears the charge and lowers the bounty. - SELF-REPORT, to confess something not yet registered. Half the usual fine, but a real charge until settled or served. - CUSTODY, to turn yourself in or to request a hearing before Eris. The custody options close the computer, because the cells and the courtroom are real places.

app_eurodemics.title: App: Eurodemics
app_eurodemics.description: The public terminal of the continental epidemic observatory, reading the live outbreak grimorie. Three pages: - SITUATION: outbreaks running, people currently ill, people dead, towns affected, the worst hit towns, and a readout of wherever you are standing right now, including whether anybody in your party has caught something. - OUTBREAKS: every outbreak currently burning, each with its daily curve, one point per day, redrawn when the model advances at midnight, over the town by town table. - ARCHIVE: outbreaks this world has already closed, plus the epidemics and mass hysterias of the last century. The graph deliberately puts people currently ill and people dead so far on one axis, because both are counts of people and they share a scale honestly.

app_artifact_analyzer.title: App: Artifact Analyzer
app_artifact_analyzer.description: Analyses the procedural artifacts you find, which is how you learn what an unfamiliar one actually does rather than guessing from its name. An artifact you have not analysed is a gamble. One you have is a tool.

app_token_exchange.title: App: Token Exchange
app_token_exchange.description: Converts euros into arcade tokens and back. It quotes the same rate as the physical converter machine in the world, so there is no advantage to using one over the other beyond not having to walk anywhere.

the_hexphone.title: The Hexphone
the_hexphone.description: The party carries a mobile phone. It holds credit, contacts, a call history, an inbox of messages, and a couple of built in games in the manner of an LCD handset. Calling a contact really calls them: it triggers what that person does when called. Incoming calls arrive with an answer or decline prompt. Controls: the keypad digits dial and act as shortcuts, the arrows navigate lists, Enter is the MENU button (select, call, open), Escape is END (back, and from the home screen it closes the phone), and backspace deletes a digit while dialling. Public PAYPHONES exist too, and share the same contacts and the same credit grimorie. A payphone only places outgoing calls: no inbox, no games, no incoming calls and no way to save a new contact.

television.title: Television
television.description: Televisions can be watched wherever you find one, and tuning into a channel teleports you into that channel's room in the studio, where the programme's cast performs the broadcast. Each named cast member turns to face you, takes their own sprite and reads their lines. A programme with no cast is narrated instead. The dialogue is generated from templates over lore banks, and it splices in the LIVE state of your world: the history channel and the news desk read back the actual simulated century and the actual current news. Every line also picks its own wording as it is spoken, so the same beat is never phrased the same way twice. The weekly schedule regenerates every in game week and is fixed for that week; the script is rerolled on every tune in, ten to sixteen exchanges per slot. OK advances, Cancel interrupts. Commercial breaks are bought by real advertisers: the segments sell either a product, quoted at its real price out of the item database, or a POSITION, paid for by one of the powers carving up the world. Finishing a transmission tops up the Fun need of everybody in the party; interrupting one pays less. Anybody with the Technophobe trait LOSES the same amount instead. The channel guide is drawn as a forty by twenty five teletext page.

the_radio.title: The Radio
the_radio.description: Radios in the world are tunable across AM, FM and EM bands, and the stations are built from the actual music files the game ships with, so every track in the game is somewhere on the dial. Left and right change frequency, up and down change band, page up and page down scan for the next station, Enter marks a favourite, Shift with left and right jumps between favourites, and Shift with up and down sets the volume. Between stations there is static. The station you were last tuned to is remembered.

music_and_sound.title: Music and Sound
music_and_sound.description: A few things about how the game sounds are worth knowing. BATTLE MUSIC is yours to choose, from the Options menu. There is a Random entry that draws a different track at the start of every fight, custom tracks included, and None if you would rather fight in silence. MAP MUSIC is seeded: one track per combination of biome, nation and time of day, drawn from wide pools, so a place has its own music and keeps it. Some music is GENERATED rather than played: a procedural music system writes it live. Whatever is playing announces itself, either as a small notification or as a procedurally drawn cassette, with the track and the artist, so you can find out what you are listening to. Footsteps change with what you are walking on.

diversions.title: Diversions
diversions.description: There is a great deal to do in this world that is not adventuring, and almost none of it is a menu. The 3D games are real simulations rendered through a retro shader, and most of them are played wherever you are standing: the pool table, the basketball court, the bowling alley and the chess board are all dropped into the scenery of the map you are on, so the same cabinet is played in a bar, in a cave or on an alien planet. Playing something feeds the FUN need of everybody in the party, which is a real mechanical reason to stop and waste an afternoon. Where a game asks for control hints, it does not print them: you are expected to try the obvious keys, which are the ones you already use. Two players can share almost all of them. With a second gamepad, or the numpad on a shared keyboard, the real time games let either player steer and the turn based ones become hot seat, even without a split screen session running.

the_arcade_cabinet.title: The Arcade Cabinet
the_arcade_cabinet.description: Arcade cabinets take TOKENS, bought with euros at the converter or on the Hypernet. A cabinet keeps high scores with the letter entry of the period, and runs a demo when nobody is playing. Every cart is a complete little game, drawn in colour ASCII: - SNAKE, against a red AI snake competing for the same apples, with a power up that doubles your speed. - MANPAC, a maze of pellets with three hunters and power pills that make them edible. - FROGGER, across roads and rivers to five home slots. - SPACE INVADERS, with destructible barriers. - ASTEROIDS, with rocks that split and a screen that wraps. - BREAKOUT, with falling capsules that widen the paddle, slow the ball or grant a life. - CENTIPEDE, winding down through a mushroom patch, splitting when you shoot the middle, with a spider that eats the mushrooms. - BUBBLE POP, colours that stick and clusters that fall. - The BOOT SEQUENCE, which is a cabinet booting up: ROM check, RAM test, sound chip, video, security, and then something you can actually walk around in.

bowling.title: Bowling
bowling.description: A full 3D alley with real rigid body pin physics, simulated in metres at real bowling dimensions: 18.29 metres to the head pin, a 1.07 metre lane, gutters, a 6.35 kilogram ball and 1.53 kilogram pins. There is no bowler model because the view is the bowler's own. The camera rides the ball down the lane and cuts to the pin deck for the strike, and a pinsetter rake sweeps the deadwood between rolls. It uses the aim, power and spin slider flow shared with pool and basketball: stop each oscillating bar where you want it.

pool.title: Pool
pool.description: A nine foot table simulated in metres, with real balls: they roll under cloth friction, throw each other off on impact, rattle in the jaws of a pocket and drop. Aim, power and spin, each set with the oscillating slider, and the table is dropped into whatever scenery you are standing in.

basketball.title: Basketball
basketball.description: A free throw shootout against a CPU opponent on a real half court measured in metres: a 4.57 metre free throw line, a rim 3.05 metres up with a 22.9 centimetre radius, and a proper backboard. The ball is a real projectile. It arcs under gravity, clatters off the rim ring, banks off the backboard and drops through the net, or does not.

chess.title: Chess
chess.description: Full rules chess on a low poly 3D board where every piece is a REAL creature from the game's own 3D battler system, dealt from the world seed, so a given world always fields the same two armies: a bright one for White and a black hearted one for Black. There are two modes: normal chess, and Chaos.

fishing.title: Fishing
fishing.description: A first person 3D fishing game, and everything that swims in it is a REAL model: fish, junk and hostile encounters are built by the same procedural battler system the battles use, so a Megalodon you hook in the lake is the Megalodon you then have to fight. You aim by looking around, a ring on the water shows where the cast will land, and then it is a contest between the line and whatever took it. Where you fish matters: what is in the water is what lives there.

surfing.title: Surfing
surfing.description: First person surfing, and the wave is not a backdrop. Every wave is a travelling swell with a tilted crest, so it PEELS: the point where it breaks races along the beach at about ten metres a second and the whitewater eats the wave behind it. There is no surfer model because you are standing in it. Below you is the board, and it pitches, rolls and slaps across the chop exactly as the physics says. The whole game is reading the peel and staying ahead of it.

the_shooting_range.title: The Shooting Range
the_shooting_range.description: A first person target range where the weapon in frame is not a picture: it is the same 3D weapon model the battle overlay raises, built, posed, aimed and fired by the real weapon system, so every gun and bow in the game handles here exactly as it does in a fight. Nothing is equipped on your character. The range hands you something over the counter and takes it back at the door, so it is also the place to try a weapon before buying one. The rack holds only what shoots: bows, projectile weapons and firearms.

the_horse_race.title: The Horse Race
the_horse_race.description: A real turf course in 3D: mown grass, running rails, a starting gate that springs open, distance poles, a winning post and a grandstand. The runners are the game's own procedural creatures, and each one is built FROM ITS OWN NAME: the name is hashed and handed to the battler system as the identity it keys a coat, a colour and a build to, so a named horse is the same horse in every world. You bet on them. The odds are honest: they are computed by simulating the actual race many times over the very same step function the race then runs, so a short price really is a likely winner.

the_monster_tournament.title: The Monster Tournament
the_monster_tournament.description: A single elimination tournament of monsters that you bet on. You pick a fighter, place your bet in tokens, and only the fights involving your monster are shown to you. The fights are REAL battles, run between two creatures by the engine itself: the AI picks their skills, pays their costs, rolls to hit, evade and crit, applies the damage formulas, inflicts states, raises buffs and ticks poison at the end of the turn. The result is then replayed for you in a 3D arena with the animations. Nothing about the outcome is decided by the betting.

slots,_scratch_cards_and_tarot.title: Slots, Scratch Cards and Tarot
slots,_scratch_cards_and_tarot.description: THE SLOT MACHINE is a real cabinet standing on the floor, and its reels are drums: each symbol is a plate on a facet of a cylinder, so a spin is the drum turning and a landing overruns its stop and springs back the way a mechanical reel does. The symbols come from the game's own icon set and each one's average colour becomes its pip in the payout table. SCRATCH CARDS are printed tickets you rub the foil off, panel by panel, in whatever order you like, and the card can be turned over in the light while you do it. The counter is a carousel of four products that turn on the spot so you can see a ticket before paying for it. THE TAROT TABLE is a real table: the deck riffles, the reader cuts it, the cards fly to their positions face down and turn over one at a time.

the_piano.title: The Piano
the_piano.description: A playable three octave keyboard, C3 to B5, played with the whole typing keyboard laid out like a tracker (two manuals, whites on one row and blacks on the row above), with a gamepad, or with the mouse. Keys light up as they sound and show the button bound to them. It is a real instrument rather than a puzzle, and playing it feeds the Fun need.

lockpicking.title: Lockpicking
lockpicking.description: Picking a lock is a falling block puzzle: a key bit has to be placed into a partly packed keyway. The difficulty of the lock decides how hard the fit is. It needs LOCKPICKS, which are consumed on a failure. A skeleton key skips the game entirely and opens the lock outright. Lockpicking is how you get into locked doors and how you steal a parked car. It is also a crime when you are caught at it.

hypertamer.title: HyperTamer
hypertamer.description: A virtual pet on a monochrome LCD handset, in the manner of the toys of the era. The pet is drawn from the game's own creature database and has a personality that changes how it behaves. It needs REAL TIME care: it eats, sleeps, plays and can die of neglect, and time passes while the game is closed, so it is still hungry when you come back. Training minigames raise its stats and it grows accordingly.

the_card_game.title: The Card Game
the_card_game.description: A collectible card game with its own collection, deck builder and duels. A CARD is a monster, a weapon or a piece of armour out of the game's own database, printed with five stats, STR, WIS, DEX, PSI and CON, each from 0 to 13. Those numbers are percentiles against that card's own roster rather than raw parameters, which is why the spread is even instead of bunched at the bottom. Equipment is bolted onto a monster already on the board and its values are added to it, clamped back to 13. A DECK is 9 to 20 cards and may only hold copies you actually own. Several decks can be kept and one is active. A player who never opens the deck builder is dealt the best legal deck their collection can make. A DUEL is three by three. On your turn you either draw three cards or place one: a monster onto a free tile, or a piece of gear onto one of your own monsters, one weapon and one armour each. The table is dressed in the monsters' own walking sprites. The moment the last tile is taken, every monster looks at its four orthogonal neighbours, picks the weakest enemy among them and fights it. Every pairing is scored against ONE frozen snapshot of the board and every death lands together, so a match is decided in a single simultaneous clash rather than a cascade. Most stats won takes the fight; an equal count destroys both. Whoever has more monsters standing wins, ties broken on the summed stats of the survivors. BOOSTER PACKS are six cards from one pool, weighted so the last of the six is never common. The other way to win a card is to CAPTURE a creature in battle. It picks the weakest one still standing and tries to bind it: mostly a question of how badly hurt it already is, helped by the caster's PSI against the creature's own, and hopeless against anything more than ten levels above your median. Success adds the card AND kills the creature, so you still get the corpse and the spoils.

the_raman_scanner.title: The Raman Scanner
the_raman_scanner.description: A spectroscopy scanner that analyses whatever object you are facing: statues, paintings, masks, bookcases and library objects. It identifies what they are made of and draws a real Raman spectrum for the material. It pays KNOWLEDGE, which makes wandering a museum a legitimate way to fund your training.

the_periodic_table.title: The Periodic Table
the_periodic_table.description: A viewer for the periodic table, laid out as a book: the full grid on the left page, including the lanthanides and actinides and a set of ESOTERIC elements that do not appear in any real table, with the selected element's description on the right.

state_arcane_surge.title: State: Arcane Surge
state_arcane_surge.description: Increases magic power but consumes MP each turn. It raises INT by 50%, raises WIS by 50% and drains 10% of max MP every turn. It lasts 3-5 actions.

state_berserk.title: State: Berserk
state_berserk.description: Increases attack power but decreases defense and makes target attack randomly. It raises STR by 50% and lowers CON by 30%. The afflicted attacks anyone at random, ally or enemy. It lasts 2-4 actions.

state_bleeding.title: State: Bleeding
state_bleeding.description: It drains 10% of max HP every turn. It does not wear off on its own. And it follows you out of the fight.

state_blind.title: State: Blind
state_blind.description: It lowers accuracy by 50%. It lasts 3-5 actions.

state_burned.title: State: Burned
state_burned.description: It drains 10% of max HP every turn. It does not wear off on its own. And it follows you out of the fight.

state_charm.title: State: Charm
state_charm.description: It carries no stat change of its own. The afflicted turns on their own side. It lasts 2-4 actions. A solid hit can break it early.

state_cold.title: State: Cold
state_cold.description: It lowers ice damage taken 50%, raises STR by 10% and raises fire damage taken 200%. It lasts 5 turns.

state_confusion.title: State: Confusion
state_confusion.description: It carries no stat change of its own. The afflicted attacks anyone at random, ally or enemy. It lasts 2-4 actions. A solid hit can break it early.

state_shadow_veil.title: State: Shadow Veil
state_shadow_veil.description: Makes target harder to hit but also reduces their accuracy. It lowers accuracy by 40% and lowers how often it is targeted by 50%. It lasts 2-4 actions.

state_silence.title: State: Silence
state_silence.description: It seals a school of skills. It lasts 3-5 actions.

state_sleep.title: State: Sleep
state_sleep.description: It lowers evasion by 100%. The afflicted cannot act at all. It lasts 3-5 turns. A solid hit can break it early.

state_static.title: State: Static
state_static.description: It lowers thunder damage taken 50% and raises STR by 10%. It lasts 5 turns.

state_stun.title: State: Stun
state_stun.description: It lowers evasion by 100%. The afflicted cannot act at all. It lasts 1-2 turns.

state_unbalanced.title: State: Unbalanced
state_unbalanced.description: Target has a chance to fail their action at the end of each turn. It lowers accuracy by 30%. It lasts 1-3 actions. A solid hit can break it early.

state_vulnerability.title: State: Vulnerability
state_vulnerability.description: Decreases the target's physical defense. It lowers CON by 50%. It does not wear off on its own. And it follows you out of the fight.

state_wet.title: State: Wet
state_wet.description: It lowers fire damage taken 50% and raises thunder damage taken 100%. It lasts 5 turns.

state_immortal.title: State: Immortal
state_immortal.description: It wards off Dead. It lasts 1-2 turns.

state_poison.title: State: Poison
state_poison.description: It drains 5% of max HP every turn. It does not wear off on its own. Walking it off works too, and it follows you out of the fight.

state_rage.title: State: Rage
state_rage.description: It raises STR by 50%. The afflicted attacks an enemy at random and cannot be commanded. It lasts 2-4 actions. A solid hit can break it early.

state_freeze.title: State: Freeze
state_freeze.description: It lowers evasion by 100%, seals a school of skills and seals a school of skills. The afflicted cannot act at all. It lasts 3 turns.

state_paralysis.title: State: Paralysis
state_paralysis.description: It lowers evasion by 100%. The afflicted cannot act at all. It lasts 3 turns.

state_locked_on.title: State: Locked on
state_locked_on.description: Increases critical rate It raises critical rate by 300%. It lasts 2-4 actions.

state_hp_regeneration.title: State: HP Regeneration
state_hp_regeneration.description: It restores 10% of max HP every turn. It lasts 4 turns.

state_mp_regeneration.title: State: MP Regeneration
state_mp_regeneration.description: It restores 10% of max MP every turn. It lasts 4 turns.

state_ap_regeneration.title: State: AP Regeneration
state_ap_regeneration.description: It restores 10% of max AP every turn. It lasts 4 turns.

state_magic_reflection.title: State: Magic Reflection
state_magic_reflection.description: It raises magic reflection by 100%. It lasts 5 turns.

state_protect.title: State: Protect
state_protect.description: It changes how the battler behaves. It lasts 1 turn.

state_provoke.title: State: Provoke
state_provoke.description: It raises how often it is targeted by 800%. It lasts 5 turns.

state_hide.title: State: Hide
state_hide.description: It stops how often it is targeted entirely. It lasts 5 turns.

state_counter_attack.title: State: Counter Attack
state_counter_attack.description: It raises counter rate by 100%. It lasts 3 actions.

state_status_ailment_block.title: State: Status Ailment Block
state_status_ailment_block.description: It wards off 9 different conditions. It lasts 5 turns.

state_inspired.title: State: Inspired
state_inspired.description: Reduces MP cost. It lowers MP cost by 75%. It lasts 5 turns.

state_hot.title: State: Hot
state_hot.description: It raises water damage taken 100%, raises STR by 10% and lowers petro damage taken 50%. It lasts 5 turns.

state_divine_shield.title: State: Divine Shield
state_divine_shield.description: Reduces all incoming damage and prevents critical hits. It lowers physical damage taken 30%, lowers fire damage taken 30%, lowers ice damage taken 30%, lowers thunder damage taken 30%, lowers water damage taken 30%, lowers petro damage taken 30%, lowers wind damage taken 30%, lowers sacred damage taken 30%, lowers cursed damage taken 30% and raises critical evasion by 100%. It lasts 3-5 turns.

state_death_mark.title: State: Death Mark
state_death_mark.description: Target receives increased damage from all sources and is more likely to be targeted. It raises physical damage taken 30%, raises fire damage taken 30%, raises ice damage taken 30%, raises thunder damage taken 30%, raises water damage taken 30%, raises petro damage taken 30%, raises wind damage taken 30%, raises sacred damage taken 30%, raises cursed damage taken 30% and raises how often it is targeted by 900%. It lasts 2-3 actions.

state_perfect_focus.title: State: Perfect Focus
state_perfect_focus.description: Guarantees critical hits but reduces defense. It raises critical rate by 100% and lowers CON by 20%. It lasts 2-3 turns.

state_ethereal.title: State: Ethereal
state_ethereal.description: Target takes no physical damage but double magical damage. It makes physical damage harmless, raises fire damage taken 100%, raises ice damage taken 100%, raises thunder damage taken 100%, raises water damage taken 100%, raises petro damage taken 100%, raises wind damage taken 100%, raises sacred damage taken 100% and raises cursed damage taken 100%. It lasts 3-5 turns.

state_life_link.title: State: Life Link
state_life_link.description: Damage taken is shared among all party members. It carries no stat change of its own. It lasts 3-5 turns.

state_nausea.title: State: Nausea
state_nausea.description: It lowers AGI by 25%. It does not wear off on its own. And it follows you out of the fight.

state_drunk.title: State: Drunk
state_drunk.description: It drains 40% of max AP every turn. It does not wear off on its own. A solid hit can break it early, walking it off works too, and it follows you out of the fight.

state_infected.title: State: Infected
state_infected.description: It drains 10% of max HP every turn. It does not wear off on its own. And it follows you out of the fight.

state_floating.title: State: Floating
state_floating.description: It raises thunder damage taken 100%, raises STR by 10%, makes petro damage harmless and lowers physical damage taken 50%. It lasts 5 turns.

state_invisible.title: State: Invisible
state_invisible.description: It raises evasion by 999%, raises magic evasion by 999%, raises critical evasion by 999% and lowers how often it is targeted by 70%. It lasts 3 turns. A solid hit can break it early.

state_oily.title: State: Oily
state_oily.description: It raises fire damage taken 899%. It lasts 5 turns.

state_dodge.title: State: Dodge
state_dodge.description: It raises evasion by 200% and raises magic evasion by 200%. It lasts 1 turn.

state_withdrawal.title: State: Withdrawal
state_withdrawal.description: It lowers STR by 15%, lowers INT by 15%, lowers DEX by 10%, lowers accuracy by 15% and lowers evasion by 5%. It does not wear off on its own. And it follows you out of the fight.

state_grappled.title: State: Grappled
state_grappled.description: Held in a lock. Agility and evasion collapse and physical blows land harder. It lowers DEX by 60%, lowers evasion by 60% and raises physical damage taken by 25%. It lasts 2-3 turns.

state_pinned.title: State: Pinned
state_pinned.description: Pinned to the ground and unable to act. One solid hit shakes it loose. It lowers evasion by 90%. The afflicted cannot act at all. It lasts 1-2 turns. A solid hit can break it early.

state_guard_broken.title: State: Guard Broken
state_guard_broken.description: Their defence is prised open: defence halved and guarding does nothing. It lowers CON by 50%, lowers WIS by 20% and stops guarding entirely. It lasts 2 turns.

state_winded.title: State: Winded
state_winded.description: The breath is gone: slower, and no stamina builds up while it lasts. It lowers DEX by 20%, lowers AP charge rate by 65% and drains 5% of max MP every turn. It lasts 3 turns.

state_combo_ready.title: State: Combo Ready
state_combo_ready.description: The opening has been read and the follow-up is loaded. Some techniques hit far harder with it. It raises accuracy by 20% and raises critical rate by 15%. It lasts 2 turns.

state_vital_exposed.title: State: Vital Exposed
state_vital_exposed.description: A vital point is uncovered. Every physical blow that follows does half again as much. It raises physical damage taken by 50% and lowers critical evasion by 30%. It lasts 2-3 turns.

state_rooted_stance.title: State: Rooted Stance
state_rooted_stance.description: Planted and immovable: much harder to hurt or knock over, and slower for it. It raises CON by 40%, lowers DEX by 30% and wards off 3 different conditions. It lasts 4 turns.

state_flow_state.title: State: Flow State
state_flow_state.description: Reading the blow before it is thrown: turns attacks aside and answers some of them. It raises counter rate by 25%, raises evasion by 20% and lowers physical damage taken by 15%. It lasts 3 turns.

state_chi_burn.title: State: Chi Burn
state_chi_burn.description: The price of spending everything at once. The body keeps paying for a while. It drains 4% of max HP every turn, lowers INT by 15% and lowers AP charge rate by 50%. It lasts 3 turns.

state_concussed.title: State: Concussed
state_concussed.description: A blow to the head. Nothing aims true and nothing thinks straight. It lowers INT by 30%, lowers WIS by 30% and lowers accuracy by 20%. It lasts 2-3 turns.

lore_the_squishing.title: Lore: The Squishing
lore_the_squishing.description: On 21 December 2012, the goddess of discord Eris will kill the goddess of justice Maat by hurling the Omega Tower at her. That has already happened, in the future. What reached this dimension was the throw's echo, sent twenty years backward and across ninety-two dimensions, landing on 21 December 1992 as dimension three's own sky, ours. The paradox has been fraying the timeline and the stability of all ninety-two dimensions ever since. From 1992 onward, spacetime began knotting itself into localized time-loop bubbles (see: the Rule of 80), and fragments of other dimensions started collapsing into this one, the Empty Empire of Varlenia foremost among them. The damage compounds: by 2012, when the throw finally lands for real, the distortion is expected to make this dimension outright uninhabitable. Squishing does not strike every dimension evenly. The higher a dimension's number, the faster it unravels, the Green Fields, dimension 77, are already largely uninhabitable. The Omega Tower, driven into the earth by the very throw that started all this, is the one thing still holding the ninety-two dimensions apart from collapsing into each other; without it, by most accounts, they already would have.

lore_the_rule_of_80.title: Lore: The Rule of 80
lore_the_rule_of_80.description: Since the Squishing began, anything that moves faster than 80 kilometers per hour is pulled into the nearest time-loop bubble, a patch of spacetime, from a few meters to hundreds of kilometers across, where the day resets at its end as if it never happened. Once inside, the rule inverts: the only way out is to move outward past 80 km/h again, and staying under that speed keeps you looping. Bubbles are nearly invisible from the outside, little more than a shimmer in the air at close range, so they are marked on every road map to keep travelers from wandering in by accident. Their number and their size have both been growing since 1992, and both keep climbing as 2012 approaches. Looping has its own grim comfort: the only way to die for good inside a bubble is to die while moving above 80 km/h, or be struck by something that is. Everything else just resets. The cost is stagnation, the mind adjusts to the repetition faster than most expect, and a looper keeps their memories of every previous day even as the world resets around them. No signal, electronic, mental, or magical, crosses a bubble's edge, which is why carrier pigeons fitted with USB drives (they can hit 90-100 km/h with a tailwind) remain the fastest reliable post between one loop and the next, and why the Truckers Society exists at all: someone has to carry people, goods, and news between communities that live in different bubbles. Bubba's liminal engine is the one known way to drive straight through a bubble without ever slowing below the threshold.

lore_the_encompassing_road.title: Lore: The Encompassing Road
lore_the_encompassing_road.description: Every road in every world of the multiverse is, underneath, the same road. Bubba's liminal engine compresses the stretch ahead of a vehicle, and correctly calibrated, it opens onto the Encompassing Road itself: a mode of travel where an ordinary highway exit can lead somewhere else entirely, another place, another dimension, another time, even the Scraps of Creation. The road predates every driver on it. Trillions of years ago, so the story goes, the concept of a road was born from the God of Asphalt, who paved the first one, and became the first victim of a hit-and-run, run down by a greater god.

lore_the_mages_guild.title: Lore: The Mages Guild
lore_the_mages_guild.description: Founded in 950 BC by King Solomon, the Mages Guild governed the world's hidden balance for millennia before Margaret Thatcher revealed the existence of magic to the entire planet, live, when she deployed it during the Falklands War. In the early 1900s the Guild was refounded by Sir Aleister Crowley under the patronage of the British royal house as a pseudo-chivalric order, which is why its leadership still carries the styles Sir and Lady. Beyond rebuilding lost technology with magic on behalf of the world's governments, the Guild's stated purpose is defending reality from extradimensional threats and the horrors the Squishing keeps letting in. Internally it is fractured into as many currents as there are schools of magic, but every major decision runs through the Three Pillars, who stand for the past, the present, and the future. As of 2001, the seats are held by Sir Aleister Crowley (the past), Lady Margaret Thatcher (the present), and 'the Father,' Shoko Asahara (the future). Holding a Pillar's seat halts its holder's aging for as long as they keep it; a Pillar's term normally runs fifty years. Crowley has never once stepped down, and nobody left in the Guild is in any position to make him, he knows spells even the gods have never heard of.

lore_hypercapitalist_collective.title: Lore: Hypercapitalist Collective
lore_hypercapitalist_collective.description: The Hypercapitalist Collective is a pyramid scheme the size of a continent, running the trade between dimensions. Its members took the Rule of 80 and made it doctrine: by staying above the threshold long enough, their bodies stopped resetting even once they finally stand still, so while the rest of the world loops and forgets, the Collective remembers everything, indefinitely. That memory is the whole business model. They sell escapes to people trapped in time loops, and they trade absolutely anything else, memories and emotions included. They also hold a monopoly on the one resource nobody can loop their way around: they control every source of clean water left, while everything outside their reach is cut with LSD. The Collective is at open war with the Archive Foundation, whose radical-transparency doctrine stands directly in the way of a trade empire built on secrecy and leverage, and stands allied with the Gods.

lore_em,_the_memory_witch.title: Lore: Em, the Memory Witch
lore_em,_the_memory_witch.description: Em was born in 1984 in Wimbledon, Britannia, wanting to be a witch in an age that had filed magic away among the fairy tales. That changed when Margaret Thatcher, who was secretly a power broker within the Mages Guild, needed a focal point for the Solomon Ritual and chose her. The ritual's price was 92% of her memories. They did not simply vanish, they were forged into the Spear of Memory, the same weapon Eris later used to kill the Father aspect of YHWH. Em woke up alone on Ritual Island on the first of January, 2001, with no past she could recall and a magical power she is still learning to hold. She has been on the road ever since, riding a camper she shares with Bubba, heading toward a meeting in Beagle that she can barely remember agreeing to.

lore_camelcase_magic.title: Lore: CamelCase Magic
lore_camelcase_magic.description: Every spell cast since the Squishing must be written and spoken in CamelCase: words run together, a capital letter opening each one. It is not stylistic, and it is not optional. FireBall works. 'Fire ball' does not, and speaking it costs the caster dearly for the attempt. Multi-word formulas belong to a different tier entirely: transcendentals, incantations powerful enough to reshape reality on command, and the exclusive province of gods. A mortal who breaks a spell into separate words has the universe read it as an attempted transcendental and bill them accordingly, anywhere from the loss of their voice to considerably worse. Grimoires make the rule visible: a spell written wrong on the page begins infecting the neighboring words with copies of itself, and a book left unburned will go on to consume whatever is left beside it. A caster's active spells are chosen while they sleep, each carrying its own cap on daily uses. Slot two spells into the same slot and they fuse into a single temporary spell for as long as it holds; permanent versions of proven combinations can be bought from vending machines, or earned through ritual.

lore_alagadda,_city_of_masks.title: Lore: Alagadda, City of Masks
lore_alagadda,_city_of_masks.description: [Archive Foundation dossier, incomplete] Alagadda does not appear on any map the Guild or the Foundation has managed to fix in place, and every field team sent looking for it has come back with a different account of how they got in, if they came back at all. What survives every retelling, and what every witness insists on repeating first, is the one rule the city enforces without exception: every visitor wears a mask, and it does not come off. Remove it, for any reason, for any length of time, and the city stops counting you as a person. The condition has a name on file, Unperson, and a description consistent across every witness: invisible, untouchable, unable to leave, drifting through streets that no longer register you exist. Total Disclosure notwithstanding, this is the entirety of what the Foundation is willing to put its name to. Field teams are advised: mask on, mask secured, mask never removed.
